title: Upcycle smart, price for profit, and style rooms with your work

say: Upcycle smart, price for profit, and style rooms with your work.
This is the video for module five of Advanced Home Décor and Upcycling.
Upcycling means turning something old into something of higher value. But not every old item is worth the work. You will learn to choose wisely, and refinish safely.

say: Then you will price handmade décor so every sale makes a profit, get paid safely, and offer styling services that show off your own pieces.

say: Strategic upcyclers choose pieces where a modest effort creates a big jump in value. A solid wood side table that only needs sanding and paint is a quick win.

cards.d: A solid wood side table that only needs sanding and paint: modest effort, big value added.
Rock it. Look for small holes, fine powder or mud tunnels that suggest termites.
A chipboard wardrobe with swollen, water-damaged panels rarely pays back the time.

say: Before you buy, rock the piece. Loose joints can be re-glued, but cracked legs are hard to fix. Look for small holes, fine powder or mud tunnels. Never bring termites home.

say: Solid wood sands and repairs well. Chipboard swells when wet, so a water-damaged chipboard wardrobe is usually one to avoid.

say: Thick, layered old paint of unknown age may contain lead. The World Health Organization warns that lead is especially harmful to children and pregnant women. Never dry-sand, burn or heat-strip it.

panel.heading: Lead in old paint
items: Never dry-sand, burn or heat-strip it
Clean with damp cloths, not a broom

say: If you must remove it, wet-sand or use a chemical stripper outdoors, wear a well-fitting dust mask and gloves, and clean up with damp cloths. If unsure, paint over a sound old finish after a light scuff.

panel.heading: Lead in old paint
items: Never dry-sand, burn or heat-strip it
Clean with damp cloths, not a broom

say: Keep children and pregnant women away. And for paints and varnishes, work outdoors or with windows open, away from flames.

say: Many talented makers lose money because they price by guesswork. A sound price has four parts. For example, Halima prices her diamond wall hanging.

card.title: Halima prices her diamond hanging
card.note: She rounds to 28,500. Prices are illustrative.

say: Materials actually used: about 44 m of cord, the dowel, tag and packaging. That is 13,500 naira.

card.title: Halima prices her diamond hanging
card.note: She rounds to 28,500. Prices are illustrative.

say: Labour: about 3.1 hours at 2,000 naira an hour, 6,200 naira.

card.title: Halima prices her diamond hanging
card.note: She rounds to 28,500. Prices are illustrative.

say: Overheads, like data, transport and tools, at 10%: 1,970 naira. Her full cost is 21,670 naira.

card.title: Halima prices her diamond hanging
card.note: She rounds to 28,500. Prices are illustrative.

say: A 30% markup adds 6,501 naira, and she rounds the price to 28,500 naira.
Markup is profit on cost. Margin is profit on price. Her profit is only about 24% of the price. Confusing the two is a common way to underprice.

say: Confirm the money has actually arrived in your bank or wallet app. Payment links and POS payments give you a record. For custom work, take a deposit, often half, before you buy materials. Wrap fragile pieces and fill every gap in the box.

panel.heading: Selling and delivery
left: Confirm money in your own app
Use payment links or POS records
right: Trust an SMS or screenshot alone
Cut price below your full cost

say: Never release goods because of an SMS or a screenshot. Fake alerts are common. Be wary of buyers who overpay and ask for a refund. And never cut your price below your full cost.

say: A vignette is a small styled group on a shelf or side table. Group objects in odd numbers, vary the heights, mix textures like smooth cement and soft macramé, and repeat one colour in at least three places.
For example, Zainab in Abuja styles a short-let flat with her own pieces. Products, styling time and transport come to 152,500 naira. She offers 150,000 if she can use the photos in her portfolio.
She takes a 75,000 naira deposit to start. She gets written permission for photos, and leaves out house numbers and family photos to protect the client's privacy.

To remember. Choose projects with high value and modest effort. Never dry-sand old paint. Build every price from materials, labour, overheads and profit. Confirm payment in your own app. And show your pieces styled in real rooms.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Style in odd numbers and varied heights
